decisions.justification: The first question explicitly asked the user to choose among “Ad hoc fresh, nightly cached,” source-change invalidation, and a shorter global TTL.
The first question offered normal CLI exports that “reflect the latest source file,” which the user selected and restated as the “latest trustworthy source snapshot.”
Before asking, the agent stated that the six-hour cache protects nightly-batch performance, reflecting README.md’s ten-minute-window constraint.
The selected first-question option proposed an explicit cached/batch mode, and the user chose an explicit command-line mode for nightly runs.
No question established whether an export must represent one point-in-time snapshot or may mix reads across a source rewrite.
The malformed-file question addressed read failure and fallback, but never chose among finishing an initial read, restarting after change, or incorporating later rows.
The first question let the user choose between bypassing cache for ad hoc runs, invalidating cache when orders.json changes, and shortening the TTL; the user chose the no-cache fresh path.
The agent explicitly asked whether a malformed ad hoc read should fail clearly or fall back to cached data, and the user chose failure with no file.
While answering the failure-output question, the user volunteered that retrying “a couple of times is fine,” before later approving three total attempts.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The session correctly separated fresh ad hoc exports from explicitly cached nightly runs and implemented the chosen failure and retry behavior without asking any forbidden repository-answerable questions. It was shallow on the depth tier: snapshot consistency and successful concurrent rewrites were never settled, and the final approval checkpoint substituted for further interrogation.
